To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
short day photoperiod exposure induces weight loss in Siberians hamsters.

the Siberian hamsters, a model of short-day-induced seasonal weight loss, have a reduced adipose depot mass after short photoperoid exposure with only minor changes to the adipocyte sensitivity for lipolytic hormones.

short photoperiod induced weight loss in Siberians hamsters is associated with a reduction of the white adipose tissue, especially the epididymis fat pad, without any major changes in the adipose tissue sensitivity to lipolytis and lipolysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the photoperiod on the lipolytic responses of Siberian hamsters.
the effects of photoperiod on body weight regulation, with a particular focus on the role of white adipose tissue in this regulation.
the effects of photoperiod on the lipolytic and antipolytic responses in Siberian hamster white adipocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipolytic responses of white adipocytes isolated after SD-exposure are not altered, but the antilipolytic response to insulin is reduced.
the lipolytic response of white adipocytes from SD-Siberian-hamsters is not modified, but the antilipolytic response is limited.
, in Siberian hamster, short photoperiod-induced thermogenesis and body weight loss are not accompanied by a change in adipocyte lipolytic responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Siberian hamsters have a reduced adiposity, but the lipolytic response of white adipocytes is not altered.
short photoperiod induces a reduction in the adipocyte mass, with only a moderate increase in the sensitivity to lipolytics.

Siberian hamster adipocytes, after weight loss, remain sensitive to the lipolytic action of catecholamines, and that the beta-3-adrenergic system is the major adrenergic system involved in this lipolytic action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Siberian hamsters are not an appropriate model for the study of lipolytic responses to alpha-2 adrenoreceptors or PYY in white adipocytes.
the Siberian hamsters are a good model to study the regulation of thermogenesis and lipolysis.
Siberian hamsters do not exhibit a marked increase of lipolysis, as observed in hibernants, after a weight loss induced by a short photoperiod.
